noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

retryable.description: Retry action if failure is a retryable c3 exception such as VersionConflict.

class.description: The class name of the native field type, parameter or return value (as marked with the "native" value type).

sourceVersion.description:
Specific version of the language required for the source code. The supported versions vary by language so for
languages that support multiple versions, this field is overridden with an enumeration. If unspecified, it is
assumed that the source code corresponds to a "base" version which is upward compatible.

sourceCodeType.description:
ECMAScript code can be a Script or a Module.

Scripts are easy to concatenate and execute because they work in a common global scope, making them perfect for
features like remixing because you can easily re-define a function without syntax errors.

Modules have different semantics, they are always in strict mode, duplicate imports and exports can cause
syntax errors and it is near-impossible to extend them in a predictable way.

The default behavior, using "Module", implies that implementors of types must fully implement the type, be it
a remix or a first time implementation and only the top-most implementation in remix order will be used.
Note that this will not allow selective overriding of functions. Rather, the entire original implementation must be
copied to the new implementation file, and then modified as needed to provide different behavior.

If you are not authoring ES Modules and you want all the type implementations to be concatenated, use
`sourceCodeType="Script"` instead.

@see https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-scripts-and-modules
